from.place: the exactness clause in the construction of the everywhere-defined exact left derived functor (Proposition Tag 05SE, LF part)

title: Everywhere-defined left derived functors are exact
statement: Let $D$ and $D'$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category], let $F:D\to D'$ be an exact functor, and let $S$ be a saturated multiplicative system in $D$ compatible with the triangulated structure in the sense of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. Let $Q:D\to S^{-1}D$ be an abstract localization with the universal property in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization] (and the derived-category specialization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]). If the left derived functor $LF:S^{-1}D\to D'$ is defined at every object of $D$ in the sense of Definition Tag 05S9, then the functor $LF$ characterized by the universal property (equation derived-equation-everywhere) is exact as a functor of triangulated categories.

source.place: Definition Tag 05S9 (definition-derived-functor) and Proposition Tag 05SE (proposition-derived-functor), LF part

proof.text: The everywhere-defined values of LF are functorial on morphisms by Lemma 05SA(2), so they define the morphism part of LF.
For every s in S, Lemma 05SB(2) says that LF(s) is an isomorphism, so the value construction factors through the abstract localization Q by its universal property.

source.place: Lemma 05SB(2) and the localization universal property

proof.text: Lemma 05SU(2) supplies canonical isomorphisms LF(X)[n] \to LF(X[n]) for every integer n, hence LF is compatible with the shift.

Applying Lemma 05SC to any distinguished triangle $(X,Y,Z,f,g,h)$ of $D$ (where $LF$ is defined at all objects) shows that $(LF(X),LF(Y),LF(Z),LF(f),LF(g),LF(h))$, with $LF(X[1])$ identified with $LF(X)[1]$ by the shift isomorphism of Step 3, is distinguished in $D'$. Thus $LF\circ Q$, with the shift isomorphisms of Step 3, sends distinguished triangles of $D$ to distinguished triangles of $D'$.

By Proposition 05R6, $S^{-1}D$ carries the triangulated structure with $[1]\circ Q=Q\circ[1]$, and every distinguished triangle of $S^{-1}D$ is isomorphic to $Q$ applied to a distinguished triangle of $D$. The shift isomorphisms of Step 3 for $LF\circ Q$ descend to $LF$ by the universal property for natural transformations in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]; an isomorphic triangle of a distinguished triangle is distinguished (TR1 in $D'$), so Step 4 shows that $LF$ sends every distinguished triangle of $S^{-1}D$ to a distinguished triangle, and $LF$ is exact.

proof_origin.place: Definition Tag 05S9, Lemma Tag 05SA, and Proposition Tag 05SE in Situation Tag 05S8

lean.statement: theorem leftDerived_exact_when_defined (D : Type u) [Category.{v} D] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D] (D' : Type u') [Category.{v'} D'] [HasZeroObject D'] [HasShift D' ℤ] [Preadditive D'] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D' n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D'] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D'] (L : Type u'') [Category.{v''} L] [HasZeroObject L] [HasShift L ℤ] [Preadditive L] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor L n).Additive] [Pretriangulated L] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated L] (F : D ⥤ D') [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] (S : MorphismProperty D) (hS : S.IsSaturatedTriangulatedMultiplicativeSystem) (Q : D ⥤ L) [Q.CommShift ℤ] [Q.IsTriangulated] (hQ : Q.IsStrictLocalizationAt S) (LF : L ⥤ D') (α : Q ⋙ LF ⟶ F) (hLF : LF.IsRightKanExtension α) (hdefined : ∀ X : D, F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedDefinedAt S hS X) : ∃ (_ : LF.CommShift ℤ), LF.IsTriangulated
